title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: You don't have to swing at every pitch. You can wait for the pitch that is right in your sweet spot—and when valuation offers no margin of safety, patience is an active position.
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway Annual Meeting

web_blocks.title: 9.1 Steelmanning Both Sides of the Aisle: Bull vs. Bear Debate

web_blocks.html: An honest verdict requires steelmanning both the Bull and Bear cases before weighing them. The **Bull steelman** rests on Costco's unmatched 'scale economies shared' flywheel [1, 7, 27]. Its 84.1 million paid members (42.3 million Executive members driving 75.2% of sales) pay $5,907 million in high-margin fees [1, 7, 27]. Those fees fund 28 net annual store openings at 21.23% ROIC, $15,817 million in CFO, and $9,382 million in FCF [1, 7, 27]. Costco holds $21.3 billion in cash before the $13.3 billion special dividend and owns 94.9% of its buildings [1, 16, 19]. With room to reach 1,200+ global clubs in Asia and Europe, bulls argue Costco deserves a 42x–46x 'staple bond' multiple [1, 16, 19].

The **Bear steelman** does not question Costco's quality; it questions the entry price and margin friction [27, 28]. At $1,102.15 ($1,094.01 Nov 23), buyers pay 53.09x trailing P/E, 43.50x forward P/E, 4.43x–4.47x PEG, and a 1.92% FCF yield [27, 28]. That trailing multiple sits 48% above Costco's 10-year mean of 35.86x [27, 28]. Meanwhile, FY2027 capex jumps 16.5% YoY to ~$7.5 billion, March wage hikes (+$1.00/hr through 2027) raise payroll costs, and the $13.3B special dividend trims net cash to ~$1.8B ex-leases (cutting FY2027 interest income) [1, 16, 23, 25]. U.S./Canada renewals dipped 60 bps off peak to 92.3% (worldwide 89.8%), accrued member rewards rose 13.4% to $3,037M, ~$500M of IEEPA tariff claims face class-action litigation, and Sam's Club Scan & Go (~40% digital share) narrows the convenience gap [1, 23, 25, 31]. If Costco's P/E slides halfway back to 38x–39x, buyers earn negative 18-month returns even with flawless execution.

web_blocks.takeaway: Both our Base Case ($990.00) and Expected Value ($992.50) sit below CMP ($1,102.15) and below support ($1,018.73–$1,081.96). Red Team stress-testing to 30x–32x ($720–$768) reinforces negative asymmetry.

web_blocks.html: Our anti-hedging rule is clear: any buy verdict (`IMMEDIATE_BUY`, `ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP`, or `WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT`) needs `target_base > entry_zone_high`. It must also offer at least 1.50:1 reward-to-risk from the support zone. With `entry_zone_high` at $1,081.96 and `stop_loss` at $966.03, risk equals $115.93 per share. Clearing 1.50:1 would demand a 12–18 month base target of at least $1,255.86 (~49.4x forward EPS). We refuse to inflate our exit multiple just to write a timid `WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT` call. Instead, we assign **REJECTED** (`TIER_0`) for new capital on **VALUATION** (`COMPOUNDER_PASS` quality; `PASS_WITH_WATCH` KPIs).

web_blocks.title: 9.4 Exact Re-Underwriting Triggers & Why We Refuse to Hedge

web_blocks.html: Strict arithmetic, not stubbornness, drives our refusal to use `WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT`. From the top of support (`entry_zone_high` = $1,081.96) to the invalidation stop (`stop_loss` = $966.03), risk is $115.93 per share [26]. A mandatory 1.50:1 reward-to-risk hurdle from $1,081.96 requires a 12–18 month target of $1,255.86, or 49.4x FY2028E EPS of $25.40. Because our honest base target is $990.00 (39.0x FY2028E EPS) and our 30x–32x Bear compression stress reaches $720–$768, even a dip to $1,018.73–$1,081.96 yields negative base-case asymmetry (-8.5% from $1,081.96) [26, 27].

Three concrete triggers would bring Costco from Discarded back onto our Active Shortlist [1, 16, 23, 25]. First, a valuation reset into **$850.00–$900.00** (~33x–35x forward EPS) restores 1.50:1+ asymmetry toward $990–$1,050+ [1, 16, 23, 25]. Second, U.S./Canada renewals climbing back toward 93.0% would show Sam's Club Scan & Go is not hurting younger cohorts [1, 16, 23, 25]. Third, sustained >13% EPS growth from retail media and global store output could lift FY2028E EPS above $27.50 [1, 16, 23, 25]. Until then, Costco stays `NOT_HELD` (0 shares) and 100% of marginal cash remains in short-duration CASH (T-bills / money market).
Re-Underwriting & Verdict Trigger: Promote COST from Discarded only on a reset to $850–$900 (~33x–35x forward EPS) or sustained >13% EPS growth lifting FY2028E EPS above $27.50.

book_paragraphs: We have reached the moment of synthesis—the point where every financial statement, warehouse walkthrough, competitive parallel, and technical chart must be distilled into an unambiguous capital allocation decision. Let us put both sides of the aisle on the table without hedging. If you are a Costco bull, your case is built on granite: 84.1 million paid households, $5,907 million in membership fees that represent half of operating profit, $15,817 million in operating cash flow, $9,382 million in free cash flow, 21.23% return on invested capital, and 94.9% ownership of warehouse buildings.

If you are a Costco bear—or simply a disciplined valuation underwriter—you do not need to predict that Costco's business will break. You only need to observe the math of $1,102.15 per share ($1,094.01 on the November 23 snapshot). At 53.09x trailing earnings, 43.50x forward earnings, 32.96x–33.24x EV/EBITDA, and a 1.92% trailing free cash flow yield, the market is paying 48% more than Costco's own 10-year average P/E of 35.86x for a business whose consensus 5-year EPS growth is 9.81%, whose capex is stepping up to $7.5 billion in FY2027, and whose net cash shrinks from ~$15.1 billion to ~$1.8 billion ex-leases after the $13.3 billion special dividend.

When you and I map out the 12-to-18 month probabilities honestly, the asymmetry simply is not there. In our Base Case (55% probability), Costco compounds EPS at 10.6% annually to $25.40 by FY2028, while its multiple eases gently from 53x to 39x—still a 9% premium to its 10-year historical average. That yields $990.00 per share, roughly 10.2% below today's price. In our Bear Case (25% probability), slower comps and wage/capex pressure compress the multiple to 34x on $24.00 EPS, yielding $816.00 (-26.0%)—and if macro rate pressure pushes the multiple down to its 30x–32x historical forward mean, Bear stress reaches $720 to $768 (-30.3% to -34.7%). Only in our Bull Case (20% probability)—where 13% EPS growth meets a 46x multiple—does the stock reach $1,220.00 (+10.7%). Weighting all three gives an expected value of $992.50, or -9.9% from $1,102.15.

Here is where institutional discipline separates itself from timid consensus: many analysts would look at a great business trading above fair value and slap a polite 'Wait for Support' label on it. Our framework forbids that hedge. Even if Costco pulls back to its technical support zone of $1,018.73 to $1,081.96, our $990.00 base-case value sits below support. To clear a 1.50:1 reward-to-risk hurdle from $1,081.96 against a $966.03 stop, we would have to invent a $1,255.86 base-case target—meaning we would be underwriting 49.4x forward earnings as a base case. We refuse to bend our valuation standards to fit a popular ticker. New capital is REJECTED (TIER_0) on VALUATION.

Let us pause on that anti-hedging math for a moment, because it is the single most important habit you and I can build as disciplined capital allocators. When a beloved company like Costco trades above fair value, the temptation is always to say, 'Let's just put it on Wait for Support at $1,019 to $1,082.' Look at what happens if you do the math honestly: buying at $1,081.96 with a structural stop at $966.03 puts $115.93 per share at risk. To earn a minimum 1.50-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio on that trade, your 12-to-18 month base-case target would have to be at least $1,255.86. On $25.40 of FY2028E earnings, $1,255.86 means underwriting a 49.4x forward P/E as your base case. The moment you inflate your exit multiple to 49x just to justify buying a support dip, you are no longer underwriting—you are rationalizing.

Instead, we keep our eyes wide open on both sides of the ledger. On the Bull side, 84.1 million paid households, 42.3 million Executive members generating 75.2% of net sales, 94.9% owned buildings, and a clear path toward 1,200+ global warehouses make Costco one of the safest operational franchises on earth. On the Bear side, U.S. and Canada renewal rates have drifted 60 basis points off their peak to 92.3%, March wage step-ups lock in higher store payroll through 2027, FY2027 capex is jumping 16.5% to $7.5 billion, accrued member rewards rose 13.4% to $3,037 million, $2,248 million of debt sits in current maturities, ~$500 million of IEEPA tariff refunds face consumer class actions, and Audit Committee member Helena Foulkes stepped down on November 7 after her election as Governor of Rhode Island.

So what exact price or fundamental shift would bring Costco back off the Discarded bench and onto our Active Shortlist? First, a valuation reset into the $850 to $900 range—roughly 33x to 35x forward earnings—where our 1.50-to-1 reward-to-risk hurdle clicks back into place naturally. Second, we want to see U.S. and Canada renewal rates stabilize and tick back toward 93%, proving that younger digital cohorts stick around as loyally as legacy members. Until Mr. Market offers that reset, our verified ledger shows zero shares held (`NOT_HELD`), and we keep 100% of marginal equity cash parked safely in Treasury bills and money market funds.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: REJECTING A GREAT BUSINESS IS A FEATURE, NOT A BUG
book_callouts.text: Rejecting Costco at $1,102.15 does not mean we dislike the business—we rated it COMPOUNDER_PASS. It means we respect your capital enough to wait until Mr. Market offers a 33x–35x forward multiple ($850–$900) where business compounding works for you rather than merely defending a 53x starting price.

book_subsections.title: Portfolio Action & Marginal Capital Redeployment
paragraphs: Checking our verified US accounts ledger confirms that Costco is NOT_HELD—we hold zero shares, so zero shares need to be trimmed or sold. Instead, the capital under review is our next marginal unit of US equity cash. With the broader US market regime in a Downtrend (38.8% above 50-DMA, 10 distribution days) and Costco rejected on valuation, we allocate 100% of that marginal capital to CASH (Treasury bills / money market).

We simultaneously evaluate our active shortlist and outside peer universe: with zero active US shortlist names currently clearing our Stage 2 support and >=1.50:1 reward-to-risk gate (0% shortlist allocation), and BJ's Wholesale Club (BJ) outside the shortlist at $104.82 (20.3x trailing P/E) requiring full 10-chapter standalone underwriting (0% allocation), patience in 100% CASH is the highest-conviction move on this board.

book_subsections.title: The Three-Horizon Discipline: Separating Admiration From Urgency
paragraphs: One of the most liberating habits in institutional investing is separating your judgment across three distinct time horizons so that you never feel pressured into a bad entry. On the Short-Term horizon (1 to 8 weeks), our stance is AVOID CHASING / NO OPTIONS EDGE: the stock is extended into the November 24 ~$31.47 ex-dividend event ($30.00 special + $1.47 quarterly) inside a Downtrend market regime, with inflated options volatility (27.9% IV vs 21.8% HV20). On the Medium-Term horizon (3 to 18 months), our stance is REJECTED (TIER_0) on VALUATION: our $990.00 base-case target and $992.50 probability-weighted expected value both sit below the $1,102.15 quote and below the $1,018.73–$1,081.96 support zone.

Yet on the Long-Term horizon (3 to 10 years), Costco sits at the very top of our ELITE WATCHLIST COMPOUNDER tier. You and I do not reject Costco because we doubt its 92.3% renewal rate or its 21.23% ROIC; we reject it today because our job is to compound your capital, not to collect trophy tickers at 53x earnings. Keep the alert set at $850 to $900, keep 100% of marginal cash earning risk-free T-bill yield in the meantime, and let Mr. Market come to you.
